correctness.rationale: Integrating the three frozen ODE components gives an exact nonsingular linear system for the finite-time averages \(X_T,Y_T,Z_T\), with only endpoint differences divided by \(T\) on the right. Boundedness makes those terms vanish, so convergence follows to the unique stated vector without ergodicity. The same three generator identities hold for every compactly supported invariant probability measure, and one-period integration gives the periodic-orbit case. Exact rational substitution independently reproduced both reported parameter specializations and the equilibrium squared magnitudes.
risks: Boundedness is assumed, not proved; the theorem does not establish chaos, existence, uniqueness, or basin properties of any attractor.

value.rationale: The three exact second moments are natural dynamical invariants of the published multistable system, not arbitrary statistics. They hold for every bounded forward trajectory and every compact stationary state and force nominally very different coexisting branches to have identical RMS amplitudes. That structural rigidity is useful for checking simulations and separating amplitude information from temporal/chaotic organization despite the short proof.
risks: It constrains only second moments and does not distinguish invariant measures sharing them.

limitations: Only bounded forward trajectories and compactly supported invariant probabilities are covered; no a priori boundedness or attractor-existence theorem is supplied.
